newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Israeli premier to visit Yeltsin March 10-12.
newsitem.headline: Israeli premier to visit Yeltsin March 10-12.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will visit Russia from March 10 to 12 for talks with Russian leaders on bilateral relations and the Middle East peace process, Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Friday.

Netanyahu will meet President Boris Yeltsin, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and the communist speaker of the State Duma lower house of parliament, Gennady Seleznyov.
"The exchange of views with Mr Netanyahu marks a continuation of the active work by Russia aimed at helping bring about an Israeli-Arab settlement," Yastrzhembsky told a regular news briefing.
Yitzhak Rabin, who was assassinated two years ago, became the first Israeli premier to visit Moscow, in April 1994. The two countries established full diplomatic ties in 1991.
Russia is trying to revive its influence in the Middle East peace process, which it co-sponsors with the United States, and last week played host to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.
Arafat said Moscow would be the venue for the next meeting of a multilateral cooperation group on the regional peace process, which includes the United States, Russia and the European Union.
Interfax news agency said the meeting would take place in late March and would also include several Middle Eastern countries.

Despite the latest diplomatic flurry, Moscow, dogged by severe economic problems, has lost much of its clout in the Middle East since Soviet times when its strong support for Palestinian self-rule helped balance Washington's pro-Israel stance.
Russia played no part in last month's U.S.-brokered peace deal under which Israel agreed to hand over 80 percent of the town of Hebron to the Palestinian Liberation Organisation.

Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, an Arabic speaker with long experience of the Middle East region, told Arafat that Russia would continue to provide economic aid to the Palestinian Authority within its limited means.
He also backed Arafat's call for a lifting of Israel's blockade of Palestinian territory, imposed following Moslem suicide bombings last year.
